svg.title: What the sideways-push result means
svg.desc: One complete simulation snapshot. Remaining catch geometry is shown; impact strength is untested.

g.text: One complete simulation snapshot. Remaining catch geometry is shown; impact strength is untested.
12.6 N ≈ the force needed to hold up 1.29 kg
Imagine holding the body steady and pushing the far end of the lid sideways.
The lid tip moved 0.89 mm sideways and rose about 0.41 mm on average in this model.

g.text: Blue = body and teeth. Orange = lid. This is the actual simulated shape; catch views are magnified.
How much extra inward movement would let each tooth pass?
Longer bar = more remaining capture in this fixed shape. All bars use the same scale.
Almost no capture remains on the left. The right still catches; complete opening and return were not established.
Sampled geometric clearance, about 0.01 mm radial resolution. No mesh/contact sensitivity or printed validation.
